mechaber/1:main: Laws of bran on Passover. Containing 3 seifim: One may not soak bran for chickens under any circumstances, nor may one scald it. {Rama: And when giving them barley or wheat to eat, one should be careful not to throw them in a wet place where they might become chametzed. (Mahariv)}
mechaber/2:main: A woman may not rub bran on her skin, even if it is dry.
mechaber/3:main: If one rubbed bran on a goose wet from water, some say the goose is forbidden. {Rama: And this is the custom regarding the chametz prohibition, which applies even in the smallest amount. One should be careful not to singe fowl with straw, lest there be wheat or chametzed grain there that imparts flavor to the fowl during singeing.}
baer-heitev/1:א: In any case. Even if one does not intend to leave it the measure of mil, l'chatchila it is forbidden to leave it even a moment, as in siman 459 seif 2:
baer-heitev/1:ב: (2) Hultin per the fact that we are not in Kein in Hesaf', Km.S. Mark 1983, 27, B. T. A. S. C. 27, a blood that has a disease in its stomach, which Korin B.A. understood that its cure is a mixture of barley or oats and placed on its stomach. And then he will throw the barley into it and it will not come to sourness by brewing. And if it is possible to do it in MP, he will do it, then he does not miss Akal. And refer to C. S. 18, C. C. and B. T. 17, there, subsection 6:
baer-heitev/1:ג: (3) damp. Even before Pesach one must be careful with this lest he miss and remain there during Pesach and refer to the 33:
baer-heitev/2:_: Dry. For we fear it will become moist afterward. It appears even if she does not rinse afterward in cold water they were stringent—Taz. See Chafetz Chayim:
baer-heitev/3:א: In the smallest amount. We fear some chametz remains in goose crevices; even if skinning, whole goose forbidden—see Or Zarua. From six hours onward, since no stringency of smallest-amount prohibition, one may be lenient—Chafetz Chayim see there:
baer-heitev/3:ב: Flavor. B'dieved permitted—Taz (for it is fruit juice and they do not say perhaps water came on them, for they permitted siman 463 roasting two sheaves—even one forbidden; see Rashba and Chafetz Chayim). Magen Avraham wrote: only when unspecified; but if known there was chametzed grain and they singed with it—forbidden; if singed with straw and later chametzed grain found in remaining straw—we do not presume forbidden; but if three found—doubt, requires study (per Taz citing Rabbeinu Yerucham YD 84 that not so except worms that multiplied from it; see Magen Avraham 467 (7)(9); see Chafetz Chayim). Pri Megadim: if hollow oat stalk found without grain—see siman 454 s.k. 1:
beer-hagolah/1:ב: Tur in name of Geonim, as above
beer-hagolah/2:_: Mishnah there; Rosh wrote there that nowadays one should refrain; so Tur in his name
beer-hagolah/3:_: Tur in name of Avi HaEzri
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (s.k. 1) In any case even if not, etc.—meaning why wrote in any case to forbid even if not leaving—learn from this:
machatzit-hashekel/2:_: (s.k. 2) And not, etc.—siman 454 s.k. 3 regarding b'dieved if scalded:
machatzit-hashekel/3:_: (Sk. 3) Efi' 20 that it will be wet later, even if a woman's body is wet now when it is rubbed by sweat, there is nothing in that. A person's sweat is not missed according to Mash C. 166, section 5, except because after the rubbing it is washed off in the cold, and they feel that it does not remove all the bran from her body. And some bran will remain on her body while she washes herself in the cold and misses, and the words of the 16th verse about this are mistaken and need the Hajj:
magen-avraham/1:א: In any case. Even if not leaving mil measure, l'chatchila forbidden even a moment as siman 459 seif 2:
magen-avraham/1:ב: And not scald. We are not expert in scalding—siman 454 s.k. 3:
magen-avraham/2:_: Even dry. We fear it will become moist afterward:
magen-avraham/3:א: That it is in smallest amount. We fear some chametz remains in goose crevices; unlike other prohibitions even with crevices do not forbid as YD 91 (Darkei Moshe)—see siman 467 s.k. 12:
magen-avraham/3:ב: Not to singe. B'dieved permitted (Taz); only unspecified; if known chametzed grain and singed—forbidden b'dieved siman 92; above siman 446; if singed straw then chametzed grain in remaining straw—we do not presume forbidden; if three found—doubt if comparable to worms YD 84 s.k. 9 presumed; however Taz wrote citing Rabbeinu Yerucham we do not say so except worms multiplying from it, not from outside—see there; here say at time all fell and only what we see remains; even if grain remained perhaps not chametzed—see siman 467 s.k. 11:
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) (a) There is no Shurin, etc. - because of Damakhmitsin as a grain itself:
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) (b) Morsen - and H. H. Sobin G.C. misses. [And above in the TNAD sign in the MB SKV we explain what is morsin and what is bran] and the husk of the straw in which the grain is placed which Korin Shperiar does not miss and as for the rest of the straw in Alma Demi:
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (3) In any case—meaning not effective to stand watching so bran not in water mil measure—for that measure is only b'dieved; l'chatchila forbidden even one moment as above siman 459 seif 2—see Biur Halacha:
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (4) (d) And not khultin - an accidental brew that boils the water nicely and then adds the flour or bran to the content and even a dakhlita does not miss a mm is forbidden because we are not familiar with the brew and as above in siman 19 sg and sb in the MB some details of the laws in this:
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (5) (e) In order not to waste, etc. - we would start from six or older, and there are those who wrote a daf before Pesach, one should be careful about this [however, he stands over them while they are eating until they have finished eating and what is left over, we will not put it in front of them] lest he misses it and remains there during Pesach:
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (6) Wet place—even if placed in dry place, good to beware not giving water to drink while barley before them; rather clean place well first then give water:
mishnah-berurah/2:_: (g) Even dry - that is, their way was to go to the bath and sweat and wash the body with mursen, and this is not careful, since the mursen did not fall off in the water, and the body itself absorbed water from it, only sweat from the heat of the bath, and the person's sweat does not miss the only need to be careful to transfer all the mursen over all her flesh before she bathes her body in water, whether in broth or in cold water, and since the women are not knowledgeable in this now Their flesh is dry. And if it has passed and it is not washed in the cold after it for a while it is known that everything has already passed or if it washes itself in fruit water it will become sick [HI]:
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (8) Wet goose—in Tur they soaked bran first in water; Mechaber ruled even dry bran only goose wet from water—novelty that even slight moisture on bird bran chametzs and goose forbidden even if not rinsed afterward except fruit juice:
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (9) Goose forbidden—because skin has many holes, bran remains; even if wants to rub and rinse afterward ineffective:
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (10) And this is custom for chametz, etc.—meaning though for other prohibitions taste of holes ineffective to forbid unless meat hot or at least cooked or roasted and absorbed deep; here for chametz forbidden in smallest amount we concern even live if chametz remains in goose holes. Later authorities wrote even if wants to skin entirely—forbidden, bran enters through skin deep into flesh:
mishnah-berurah/3:ד: (11) That it is in smallest amount—since main reason is smallest-amount prohibition, from six hours until Passover nullified in sixty, may permit goose with good rubbing and rinsing in water provided eat before Passover lest something visible remains and revives on Passover; some lenient even eat during Passover where great loss:
mishnah-berurah/3:ה: (12) Not to singe, etc., wheat or chametzed grain—meaning water fell after detachment and it chametzed; later authorities agreed all this is mere l'chatchila caution; from basic law even if wheat there we do not presume chametzed; even if known chametzed, do not forbid since bird not touching grain holding it from above and flame rises below. If empty stalk found dissolved in food, do not concern perhaps chametzed grain in stalk fell and dissolved:
turei-zahav/1:_: Even dry. We fear some remains when she rinses in water; and do not say from end siman 450 permitting heating hot water in chametz vessel on Passover to wash—for there no benefit from vessel absorption; here chametz visible and woman benefits rubbing. Appears even if rinse afterward in cold they were stringent lest not rinse well:
turei-zahav/2:_: Goose forbidden—because skin has cracks. In skin and gravy if cracks forbidden:
turei-zahav/3:_: and will give flavor to poultry. And in retrospect, it is not forbidden to water the fruits of the Ninhu, and there are no chametzs, and there is no reason for it to come on the same straw once.
